newsitem.title: USA: Gore would attend a Boeing event in China.
newsitem.headline: Gore would attend a Boeing event in China.

text.p: U.S. Vice President Al Gore would be willing to take part in any event announcing that China will make a major purchase of jets from Boeing Co, provided a contract has been finalized first, a senior U.S. administration official said on Thursday.
Gore leaves Saturday for a 3-nation Asian tour including a stop in Beijing for talks with top Chinese officials.

"If the Chinese tell us that they are ready to go and Boeing says there really is a contract, the vice president will be pleased to be there when the contract is signed," the official, who asked not to be identified, told reporters.

Boeing has been negotiating a major contract to sell passenger aircraft to China. The Chinese have invited Gore to take part in any announcement but the vice president's staff had been debating whether attending would suggest that Gore is trading political influence for commercial contracts.

They feared that attending such a commercial announcement would draw attention to the growing controversy in Washington over allegations China tried to influence the 1996 U.S. election with campaign contributions.
But the senior official said it would be a good thing if Boeing secures the contract, and Gore's policy is to promote the commercial interests of the United States.
